open_points.subject: OwnerSession disclosure classification
open_points.text: The table classifies “the owner session, but for its uploaded import file” as `business_confidential`, while M11 adds a pending confirmation containing “the inputs it is bound to”; A16 binds an import confirmation to names and Customer values that the same table classifies as `personal_data`.
open_points.question: What class applies to personal-data values copied into a pending confirmation: does the owner session inherit `personal_data`, or must it retain only a digest or other non-personal binding?
options: Class the pending confirmation and its containing session as `personal_data` when its bound inputs contain personal data.
Store only digests or opaque references to the mapped inputs, keeping the pending confirmation `business_confidential`.
Treat the bound inputs as an explicit second exception alongside the uploaded file.
open_points.default_guess: Store authenticated digests of the complete bound inputs and keep the raw personal values only in the uploaded file and rendered mapping.

open_points.subject: Create replay after erasure or anonymisation
open_points.text: A01 says “a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create,” while R0-36 says a repeated create “never silently makes a second project, customer or room” and the primary action says “a retried create never makes a second project.”
open_points.question: After erasure, anonymisation or whole-project deletion removes the original request id, must a later call with that id remain a replay, be refused, or create a new record?
options: Create a new record as A01 rule 8 states.
Keep a non-personal request-id tombstone and refuse or replay the later call.
Reserve the request id permanently but answer that its original record no longer exists.
open_points.default_guess: Follow the explicit State 2 rule and treat it as a new create.

open_points.subject: Kernel ending an agent session
open_points.text: A12 says “Ending a session states the current version,” but its stale-version rule names only “The owner's actions on a session”; A11 also lets Cabinet Kernel end a session without saying whether Kernel supplies or is checked against an access version.
open_points.question: Must Kernel's end-session call state the access version, and is it refused as stale if a request or owner action changed the session meanwhile?
options: Kernel states the version and a stale version refuses the end.
Kernel states no version and always ends the currently registered session.
Kernel states a version for diagnostics, but Registry does not stale-check it.
open_points.default_guess: Require Kernel to state the version and stale-check it like the owner's end action.

open_points.subject: Concurrent owner sessions
open_points.text: A13 says the owner “receives an owner session” at sign-in and lists how “the session” ends, but says nothing about existing owner sessions when the owner signs in again or signs out.
open_points.question: May several owner sessions exist simultaneously, does a successful sign-in replace earlier sessions, and does sign-out end only the presenting session or all of them?
options: Allow independent simultaneous sessions; sign-out ends only the presenting session.
Allow only one session; each successful sign-in ends the previous one.
Allow several sessions but provide both current-session and all-session sign-out semantics.
open_points.default_guess: Allow independent simultaneous sessions and make sign-out end only the presenting session.

open_points.subject: Owner-session cookie policy
open_points.text: The cookie is described only as one “that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin.”
open_points.question: What exact host/domain, path, Secure and SameSite behavior enforces “only to Registry's own origin,” including local HTTP access and cross-site requests?
options: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to the owner-interface path.
Use a host-only, HttpOnly, conditionally Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie.
Leave SameSite and path at framework defaults and rely on CSRF validation.
open_points.default_guess: Use the narrowest owner-interface path, a host-only HttpOnly cookie, Secure whenever HTTPS is used, and SameSite=Strict.

open_points.subject: CSRF and confirmation values
open_points.text: A13 requires “the CSRF protection bound to its session” and a “one-time” confirmation value Registry made, but gives no generation, entropy, comparison or exposure rules for either value.
open_points.question: Must these values be cryptographically unpredictable, how long must they be, must comparison be constant-time, and may either appear in a URL or diagnostic?
options: Require cryptographically random values of a stated minimum entropy, constant-time comparison, and no URL or diagnostic exposure.
Use UUID values with ordinary equality comparison.
Leave generation and comparison to the implementation framework.
open_points.default_guess: Use at least 256 bits from a cryptographically secure generator, compare in constant time, and never place either value in URLs, logs or diagnostics.

open_points.subject: No-op audit erasure
open_points.text: A15 rule 6 says an erasure that removes no entry “writes no entry,” but its formal invariant says every accepted `erase(d)` leaves “the erasure entry e.”
open_points.question: Is the formal invariant conditional on at least one old entry being removed, or must every accepted erasure write an entry?
options: Write an erasure entry only when at least one entry was removed.
Write an erasure entry for every accepted erasure, including a no-op.
Refuse an erasure that would remove nothing.
open_points.default_guess: Make the invariant conditional: a no-op is accepted without an entry, as rule 6 and A14 require.

open_points.subject: Imported project names and aliases
open_points.text: A16 says the mapping shows “the display name and alias each will arrive under,” but requires owner input only for each new Customer; R0-85 says the owner “may give each a new display name and an alias,” while R0-82 says projects imported under a person's name are renamed in the import.
open_points.question: For each picked project, must the owner explicitly supply a nonblank display name, when may the source name be retained, and is an omitted alias cleared or copied from the source?
options: Require an explicit nonblank display name for every picked project and treat alias as an optional explicit value.
Default both fields from the source unless the owner overrides them.
Require a new name only when the owner identifies the source name as personal, and otherwise retain it.
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to confirm an explicit nonblank display name for every picked project; accept an explicitly absent alias.

open_points.subject: References from picked records to unpicked projects
open_points.text: A16 checks only picked projects and calls a record malformed when “it names a project or room the file does not hold”; it does not say what happens when a picked room or pointer names a project that the file holds but the owner did not pick.
open_points.question: Must every imported room and pointer name its picked parent project, or can a picked import bring a child whose named project is present only in the unpicked part of the file?
options: Refuse unless every imported room and pointer names a picked project and appears under that same project.
Automatically add the referenced project to the picks.
Import the child while leaving its project unimported.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the import as malformed unless every imported child belongs to a picked project.

open_points.subject: Imported pointer status history
open_points.text: A16 rejects “more than one” published pointer and certain superseded ordering, but permits no published pointer or a published pointer below a newer superseded pointer, even though M05 says v1 imported no withdrawals and A07 publication leaves the newest version published.
open_points.question: For each imported project and type with pointers, must exactly one pointer be `published` and must it be the highest version?
options: Require exactly one published pointer and require it to have version n.
Allow no published pointer, but require any published pointer to be the highest version.
Accept any status arrangement satisfying only A16's stated checks.
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one published pointer, at the highest version, because the source had no withdrawal transition.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption format
open_points.text: A18 says each backup “is encrypted with the backup key” and “cannot be read without the key,” but specifies no authenticated-encryption construction, nonce handling, file format, key identifier or corruption/authentication rule.
open_points.question: What encryption and authentication format must every release use, and how does restore select the old key after rotation?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with a unique nonce and key identifier.
Use platform-provided whole-file encryption without a Registry-level format.
Allow each release to choose an encryption scheme, provided its own checks pass.
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AES-256-GCM envelope with a fresh random nonce and a non-secret key identifier recorded in the header.

open_points.subject: Failed daily run across restart
open_points.text: A18 says “there is at most one run per UTC day,” a failed operation is retried “at the next run,” and a missed run is made at startup “if no backup was made that UTC day”; it defines no durable fact recording that an unsuccessful run was already attempted.
open_points.question: Does a failed attempt consume that day's single run, and how does Registry preserve that fact across a restart when no successful backup exists?
options: A failed attempt consumes the day; persist the last attempted UTC date separately.
Only a successful backup consumes the day, so startup may retry failures on the same date.
Allow one scheduled attempt and one catch-up attempt after each restart.
open_points.default_guess: Count a failed attempt as the day's run and persist an atomic last-attempted date in the backup location.

open_points.subject: Reapplying privacy state after restore
open_points.text: A18 tells the owner to repeat “every erasure, restriction and end of a relationship made after the backup,” but omits later lifts and resumptions and does not say whether actions are replayed chronologically or only the final state is restored.
open_points.question: If a post-backup restriction was later lifted, or an ended relationship was later resumed, what state must the owner re-establish after restore?
options: Replay every relevant privacy transition, including lifts and resumptions, in chronological order.
Apply only the final effective privacy state recorded outside Registry.
Repeat only erasures, restrictions and ends, leaving conservative extra restrictions or ended marks.
open_points.default_guess: Re-establish the final effective state from the external retention record, including lifts and resumptions; erasures remain terminal.

open_points.subject: Security-review catalogue
open_points.text: A21 declares the review complete for “the nine of the Workbench's security review” and relies on `skills/spec-authoring/SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` for the questions, but those questions are not present in the accepted design texts.
open_points.question: What exact, versioned category questions must later reviewers and release checks use to verify that A21 is complete and determine when it must be reopened?
options: Copy the complete catalogue and its version into the accepted design.
Make the cited catalogue a versioned normative release input available to every later state.
Treat the listed category names alone as the entire catalogue.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the review as unverifiable until the exact versioned catalogue and its questions are included as normative input.
